raw_response:
I'm 56 this year. I've been on this land for 35 years, since my father handed me the hoe. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those government pamphlets much. I learn by watching — what happened on my own fields, and what Lao Wang and the others are doing. My two sons work at a factory in Handan, send some money home, but I have six mouths to feed including my old mother. Every yuan I spend on inputs is a yuan I don't have for medicine or for my granddaughter's school fees. I can't afford to gamble.

I have 12.4 mu total. Eight mu I do wheat-maize double crop, same as always. The other 4.4 mu I plant cotton — my wife is good at picking, and the cotton price at the county buyer has been steady, so I keep it. The wheat went in last October. I used mostly seed I saved from the year before, mixed with one bag of new hybrid seed because saved seed weakens after two years. I put down base fertilizer then — about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's April, the wheat is greening up, and at Qingming I topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu, roughly 10 kg of nitrogen. I irrigate three times for wheat: spring revival, jointing, and grain filling. The well water is metered now, costs more every year, so I don't waste it. Last year I got 380 kg/mu because of that dry May. This year looks about normal, so I hope for 400 kg/mu. I spray herbicide once and fungicide once if I see rust.

Cotton I'm planting this week, late April. I plow that field twice — deep first, then shallow. Cotton needs attention. I put compound fertilizer in the furrows before planting, about 15 kg per mu, then topdress once when it flowers. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is scorching. Aphids and bollworms are the enemy, so I spray insecticide three times and herbicide once. It's a lot of work — 4.4 mu doesn't sound like much but cotton is all hand labor. My wife and I do most of it, but at picking time I hire three days of help from the village women.

After wheat harvest in early June, there's no time to rest. I hire the custom planter — 30 yuan per mu — to put maize in the same week, sometimes the day after cutting wheat. No time for plowing, just plant into the stubble. I use hybrid seed, about 35 yuan per mu. Fertilizer all goes down at planting — one application of about 16 kg nitrogen per mu, I buy the compound bag from the supply shop and don't think too hard about the exact numbers, one bag does about three mu. Summer rains usually help, so I irrigate twice for maize, three times only if it's very dry. I spray herbicide once. I expect 450 kg per mu if the weather is fair.

I thought about buying more fertilizer this year because the shopkeeper said prices dropped, but I decided no. I have 4,600 yuan budgeted for all inputs. My sons sent 8,000 yuan home last month, but my mother needs her medicine and we must keep cash aside. Better to apply a little less and have money in my pocket than to risk running dry. That's how I've survived 35 years — don't change what works, keep some cash under the mattress, and watch what the neighbors do.
